evidence.title: Helsinki–Riihimäki railway
evidence.text: Helsinki–Riihimäki railway is a railway running between the Helsinki Central railway station and the Riihimäki railway station in Finland.

evidence.title: Helsinki–Riihimäki railway
evidence.text: It was opened in 1862 as a part of the Finland's first railway between Helsinki and Hämeenlinna.

evidence.title: Helsinki–Riihimäki railway
evidence.text: The Helsinki commuter rail system also runs by the Helsinki–Riihimäki railway.

evidence.title: The Wise Woman of Hoxton
evidence.text: The Wise Woman of Hoxton is a city comedy by the early modern English playwright Thomas Heywood.

evidence.title: The Wise Woman of Hoxton
evidence.text: It was published under the title "The Wise-Woman of Hogsdon" in 1638, though it was probably first performed c. 1604 by the Queen's Men company (of which Heywood was a shareholder), either at The Curtain or perhaps The Red Bull.

evidence.title: The Wise Woman of Hoxton
evidence.text: The play is set in Hoxton, an area that at the time was outside the boundaries of the city of London and notorious for its entertainments and recreations.

evidence.title: The Wise Woman of Hoxton
evidence.text: The Victorian critic F. G. Fleay suggested that Heywood, who was also an actor, originally played the part of Sencer.

evidence.title: The Wise Woman of Hoxton
evidence.text: It has often been compared with Ben Jonson's comic masterpiece "The Alchemist" (1610)—the poet T. S. Eliot, for example, argued that with this play Heywood "succeeds with something not too far below Jonson to be comparable to that master's work".

evidence.title: Summerseat railway station
evidence.text: Summerseat railway station is a preserved railway station that serves the village of Summerseat in Greater Manchester, England.

evidence.title: Summerseat railway station
evidence.text: It is part of the Heritage East Lancashire Railway (which runs for 12 miles from Heywood-Rawtenstall).

evidence.title: Rawtenstall to Bacup Line
evidence.text: The Rawtenstall to Bacup railway line opened in two stages, from Rawtenstall to Waterfoot in 1848, and from Waterfoot to the Bacup terminus in 1852.

evidence.title: Rawtenstall to Bacup Line
evidence.text: There were stations at Rawtenstall, Cloughfold, Stacksteads and Bacup.

evidence.title: Rawtenstall to Bacup Line
evidence.text: The line was doubled in 1880, at the same time as the line from Bacup to Rochdale was also opened (closed 1947).

evidence.title: Rawtenstall to Bacup Line
evidence.text: Passenger and freight services operated until the Beeching cuts in 1966, the last passenger train running on December 5th 1966 and the track being lifted in 1969.

evidence.title: Don River Railway
evidence.text: The Don River Railway is a volunteer run vintage railway and museum in Don, a suburb of Devonport, Tasmania.

evidence.title: Don River Railway
evidence.text: It runs a passenger train ride from Don to Coles Beach and return using part of the former Don River Line that ran between Don Junction and Paloona.

evidence.title: Don River Railway
evidence.text: The service is usually run Wednesday through to Sunday inclusive.

evidence.title: Don River Railway
evidence.text: Don River Railway is open every day except Good Friday and Christmas Day.

evidence.title: Don River Railway
evidence.text: On operating weekdays, customer can expect to ride in either a 1940s ex TGR rail car, or diesel locomotive pulling heritage carriages, whilst steam locomotives usually run on weekends.

evidence.title: Don River Railway
evidence.text: The railway also runs a number of diesel locomotives numbered V2, X4, Y6 and 866.

evidence.title: Don River Railway
evidence.text: Numerous other locomotives and rolling stock are in the process of being restored at the on-site workshop.
